title: Cloud Billing Budget Alerts and Anomaly

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `gcp:billing` events with `matching activity` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.3.19 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `gcp:billing` traffic without `matching activity`. Confirm UC-4.3.19 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`gcp:billing` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.19_cloud_billing_budget_ale_19"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.3.19 — Cloud Billing Budget Alerts and Anomaly: queries Google Cloud `gcp:billing` for configured audit predicates and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, cost anomalies and waste patterns for 'Cloud Billing Budget Alerts and Anomaly' erode FinOps guardrails and often reveal compromised accounts mining resources or forgotten idle infrastructure. UC-4.3.19 drives medium-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable billing export. Ingest daily/monthly cost data. Create budget alerts and forward to Splunk. Calculate baseline and alert on 2-sigma anomaly by service or project.
visualization: Line chart (cost with threshold), Table (service, cost, anomaly), Stacked area (cost by service).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `gcp:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable billing export. Ingest daily/monthly cost data. Create budget alerts and forward to Splunk. Calculate baseline and alert on 2-sigma anomaly by service or project.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="gcp:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.19_cloud_billing_budget_ale_19"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `gcp:billing` in `index=gcp` to detect cloud billing budget alerts and anomaly. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_19_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (cost with threshold), Table (service, cost, anomaly), Stacked area (cost by service)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud billing budget alerts and anomaly so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
